dataset.name: IBM Telco Customer Churn
dataset.description: Fictional telecommunications customers created by IBM as sample data.

class_imbalance.strategy: No resampling or class weights, so predicted probabilities stay calibrated; the decision threshold is tuned instead.

selection_rule: Highest cross-validated PR-AUC on the training split; among models within 0.005 PR-AUC of the best, the simplest / most interpretable is chosen. PR-AUC is used because the business cares about finding the minority churn class; ROC-AUC, F1 and Brier score are reported alongside.

threshold.method: Threshold maximising F1 on 5-fold out-of-fold predictions of the training split (never tuned on the test set).

error_analysis.false_positive_meaning: Customers flagged as likely to leave who actually stayed. Cost: a retention offer or call spent on someone who would have stayed.
error_analysis.false_negative_meaning: Customers who left but were not flagged. Cost: lost revenue with no chance to intervene. The F1-tuned threshold accepts more false positives to catch more of these.

shap.note: SHAP describes how the model uses each input; it does not prove that a factor causes a customer to leave.

tenure.label: Tenure
tenure.help: How many months the customer has been with the company.

MonthlyCharges.label: Monthly charges
MonthlyCharges.help: The amount the customer is billed each month.

TotalCharges.label: Total charges to date
TotalCharges.help: Everything billed so far. Usually close to tenure × monthly charges.

Partner.label: Has a partner
Partner.help: Customer has a spouse or partner.

Dependents.label: Has dependents
Dependents.help: Customer has children or other dependents.

MultipleLines.label: Multiple phone lines
MultipleLines.help: Has more than one phone line.

StreamingTV.label: Streaming TV
StreamingTV.help: Streams TV through the internet service.

StreamingMovies.label: Streaming movies
StreamingMovies.help: Streams movies through the internet service.

Contract.label: Contract
Contract.help: Length of the customer's current contract.

limitations: Trained on IBM's fictional Telco sample data; patterns may differ for a real business.
Probabilities are estimates from historical patterns, not certainties.
SHAP explains the model's behaviour, not proven causes of churn.
Correlated inputs (tenure and total charges) can share or offset credit in the explanation.
The model does not see complaints, usage, competitor offers or customer feedback.
